field_verifications.proposed_value: Nasopharyngeal aspirates were collected by trained site investigators using the same standardized protocol utilized in a previous cohort study of children with bronchiolitis ( 4 , 20 ). All sites used the same collection equipment (Medline Industries, Mundelein, IL) and collected the samples within 24 hours of hospitalization. The nasopharyngeal sample was added to transport medium, immediately placed on ice and then stored at −80°C. Frozen samples were shipped in batches on dry ice to Baylor College of Medicine, where they were tested for: 1) 17 respiratory viruses (e.g., respiratory syncytial virus [RSV], rhinovirus) by using real time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays ( 4 , 20 , 21 )
